historical_record.description: Completed as the Pacific Telephone Building, a 26-storey office tower then the tallest building in San Francisco and the foremost example of Art Deco architecture in the Central SoMa area. Its design, like the Chronicle building's, shows the influence of Eliel Saarinen's 1922 drawing for the Chicago Tribune Tower.
Recorded in the city's 2008 survey of the Transit Center District, adopted in 2012, as a contributor to the proposed New Montgomery, Mission & Second Historic District.

building.name: Pacific Telephone Building

historic_survey.note: The Pacific Telephone and Telegraph Building, designed by Timothy Pflueger and built 1924-1925 — the statement's opening exemplar of Art Deco in San Francisco.
